cases.name: syn-2-0001
cases.input: Okay, so the blog post is going to be about the Harlow Street invoice dispute, and I want to open with the hook right away: a three-week fight over four thousand two hundred dollars that ended with a client calling me "unreasonable" in writing. Which, honestly, is a great opener because it's exactly what everybody's afraid of. So the first section is the setup, the email from Dana Whitfield at Brightline Design dated March 14th, saying the logo revisions were "out of scope" and she wasn't paying for round four. Then section two, and this is where I really want to get into the contract. We had a signed statement of work from February 2nd, and it said three revision rounds, but it didn't define what a revision was. Is it a full redo? A color tweak? I have to explain that gap without sounding defensive, because it was partly my fault for writing it loosely. Section three is the timeline. I'll pull the actual dates: the kickoff call on February 9th, the first mockups on the 21st, the rounds on February 28th, March 5th, and March 11th. I want a little table or at least a clean list, even though this is dictated, so readers can see how it piled up. Section four is how we resolved it. Dana and I got on a call on March 19th, I offered to split the difference at thirty-one hundred, she countered at thirty-five, and we landed at three thousand eight hundred. Lessons after that, and then a sign-off inviting readers to share their own horror stories in the comments.

cases.input: Okay, so, hi Marcus, it's Dana, and I'm going to talk fast because I've got about four things in my head at once. This is for the sleep schedule project for Owen, he's our son, he's four and a half, and we need a printable chart that a freelancer can build out. Nothing fancy, but it has to be really clean. The chart needs to cover the week of March 10th through March 16th, and then it needs a blank template we can reuse every week after that. Each day gets a row, Monday through Sunday, and the columns are bedtime, wake time, nap start, nap end, and a little notes box. Oh, and put a spot for the sleep sack or the stuffed rabbit, his name is Biscuit, because Biscuit matters to him more than anything. Bedtime target is 7:30 p.m. on weekdays and 8:00 on weekends, and wake-up window is between 6:45 and 7:15 in the morning. If he wakes before 6:30 we want that flagged in red, like a quick visual thing. Naps are optional now, he's dropping them, so the nap columns can be grey-shaded by default and only light up when we actually fill them in. Deliverable is a PDF, letter size, and an editable version in Google Sheets. Budget is around 300 dollars, and I need it by Friday, March 14th, end of day. Send me a rough draft by Wednesday so I can react. Thanks so much, bye, bye!

cases.name: syn-2-0022-longest
cases.input: Okay, so this is for Dana, the freelancer I'm hoping to bring on for the billing dispute. I need to be clear up front, because the last two people I worked with went off in their own direction and I ended up redoing everything myself. So let me walk through exactly what I need, and I want you to read it back to me before you start. The problem is our electricity bill from Harbor Point Energy. The account is in my name, it's for the unit at 418 Alder Street, and the billing period was March 3rd through April 2nd. The bill came in at $847.16, which is almost three times what we paid last spring for the same unit. We did not add a space heater, we did not get a new appliance, and nobody else has moved in. Something is wrong and I want it found. Here's what I need you to do first. Pull every bill from the past twelve months from our online portal. The login is under the email address on file, and the password reset goes to my phone, so if you get locked out, message me and don't try guessing. Download each PDF and save them in a folder called Alder Billing, with the month in the filename. I don't want a summary yet, I want the raw documents. Second, compare the meter readings. Each bill lists a previous reading and a current reading. I want you to check that the difference between them matches the kilowatt-hours billed. Last time, the numbers didn't line up on the February bill, and nobody at Harbor Point ever explained why. If the math is off, I want that written down with the exact figures, not a general impression. Third, I need you to call the utility. The customer service number is on the back of the bill, and the reference for this complaint is HP-2291-K. Ask for a supervisor if the first person can't explain the meter reading. Ask specifically whether a technician has ever visited 418 Alder Street since January. Get the name of everyone you speak to and the time of the call. Write it all down in a notes file, and do not agree to anything over the phone, including a payment plan, until I've seen the notes. Fourth, check the rate schedule. The bill says we're on a residential tiered plan, but I think we were moved to a time-of-use plan in February without notice. If that's true, the charges would be calculated differently, and I want to know exactly which date the change happened. Deadline: I need a written summary by Friday, May 9th, by noon. That gives me time to file the formal dispute before the payment due date of May 20th. If we miss that window we lose the right to contest the charge, so this is the real deadline, not a suggestion. Budget is three hours total, billed at the rate we agreed. If you think it's going to run over, tell me before you exceed it, not after. Last thing. When you send me the summary, put the findings first and the explanation second. I don't need a story about how you got there. I need to know whether the meter is wrong, whether the rate changed, and what the correct amount should be. Got it? Okay. Read that back to me.
